I am fifty-eight and I never went to school. This plot is only a small corner of ground that my family owns, and I plant cassava here with some maize in between like last season. I will not buy any chemical fertilizer because one bag is too much money for this little land, and I will use my own cassava stems saved from last harvest, not the new ones they sell in town. My daughters and I will do all the work ourselves — clearing, planting, weeding, and digging — so I will not pay for any labor, and I will put some chicken droppings and sweepings from the compound on the mounds because that costs nothing.
